clue.text: University can back assembly

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for can backwards

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A college might be able to support a gathering of students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' signals the turnaround; 'can' looks like a verb but is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit can be a fitted assembly, as in a kitchen unit put together from parts.

clue.text: Rope going up without delay on execution's beginning?

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: soon means without delay, before long

indicators.note: the beginning of execution's is its first letter

explanation.surface: A hangman's rope, hastily rising at the start of an execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' reverses SOON to NOOS; 'beginning' supplies the E of execution's.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a looped rope with a running knot, as used by a hangman.

clue.text: A stress developed about parking invasion

indicators.note: about means the anagrammed letters are wrapped round the parking letter
developed suggests the letters of a stress have grown into a new form, an anagram

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Tension built up over parking intrusions, a familiar neighbourhood grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges A STRESS to TRESASS; 'about' puts it round P.
explanation.definitionFit: Trespass is unlawful entry onto another's land, an intrusion or encroachment.

clue.text: Place of safety unknown in a squalid urban area

indicators.note: in says the unknown letter sits inside the a-plus-slum letters

parts.note: a slum is a squalid run-down urban area
in algebra y is an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A refuge found by someone nameless in a city slum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts Y inside A SLUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum is protection or refuge, such as that granted to political refugees.

clue.text: Primarily urban precinct, territory of wealthy natives?

definitions.text: Primarily urban precinct, territory of wealthy natives?

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of each of the following words in turn

explanation.surface: A description of an affluent city district where the rich residents live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primarily' takes the initials of the six words that follow; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage uptown is the residential, often affluent, part of a city away from downtown.

clue.text: Model of Greek sea god only half complete

indicators.note: only half complete means we keep just the first half of the god's name

parts.note: Poseidon is the Greek god of the sea

explanation.surface: A statue of the sea god left unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half complete' keeps the first four of POSEIDON's eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To pose is to sit as an artist's model, holding a position.

clue.text: Showing a certain incorruptibility unusual for Proust

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of for Proust appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Praising the French novelist Proust for rare moral integrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges FOR PROUST. 'incorruptibility' looks moral but here means resistance to corrosion.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustproof metal resists corrosion, a literal kind of being incorruptible.

clue.text: Wallet for holding pound notes

indicators.note: holding says the word for contains the following letters

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra
D and E are two musical notes

explanation.surface: A wallet used to keep banknotes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is the containment signal; 'notes' looks like banknotes but means musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A folder is a folding cover or wallet for holding loose papers.

clue.text: Heavy burden very well carried by you once

indicators.note: carried by says the very-well letters are held inside the old word for you

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
OK means very well, as in agreement

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned assurance that a heavy load is being borne well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried by' is the containment signal; 'you once' points to an archaic pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A yoke is figuratively an oppressive burden, from the wooden frame on draught animals.

clue.text: Poisonous bacteria girl found on fish

indicators.note: in an across clue, found on means the girl comes after the fish

parts.note: a salmon is a fish
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Food poisoning traced to a girl's fish supper.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'found on' means placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: Salmonella is a genus of bacteria causing food poisoning.

clue.text: Tend to look back

indicators.note: back tells us the word for look is read in reverse

parts.note: a peek is a quick look

explanation.surface: People often glance behind them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses PEEK.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep animals or a garden is to tend or look after them.

clue.text: Manage commercial unit in church

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, an ad

indicators.note: in says the unit letter goes inside the word for church

parts.note: a minster is a large or important church
I, the Roman numeral one, is a unit

explanation.surface: Running a business section within a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the containment signal; 'unit' is the Roman numeral one.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer an organisation is to run or manage its affairs.

clue.text: I am papa's naughty child

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A father confessing he has a mischievous child.
explanation.definitionFit: An imp is a mischievous little devil, used of a cheeky youngster.

clue.text: Throttling killer disposing of line is not so normal

indicators.note: disposing of says the line letter is thrown out

parts.note: a strangler kills by throttling

explanation.surface: A murderer getting rid of a rope is hardly ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposing of' removes L from STRANGLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranger is the comparative of strange, meaning more unusual or odd.

clue.text: Boasting when leading Conservative is ousted and getting into an argument

indicators.note: is ousted means that letter is removed

parts.note: crowing means boasting gleefully

indicators.note: leading asks for the first letter of the word Conservative

explanation.surface: A political tale: a Tory leader deposed amid boasting and a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is ousted' drops C (Conservative's first letter) from CROWING. ROWING rhymes with cow, as in quarrelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowing, said to rhyme with cowing, means quarrelling noisily.

clue.text: A person who adores quarrel over sender of items abroad

indicators.note: over here means turned over, so the quarrel word is written backwards

parts.note: a row is a quarrel
a shipper sends goods overseas

explanation.surface: A devotee falls out with an export agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' signals the turnaround of the quarrel word.
explanation.definitionFit: A worshipper is one who reveres or venerates, as a deity or idol.

clue.text: Know instinctively dweller in the far north retains temperature

indicators.note: retains says the Arctic dweller holds the temperature letter within

parts.note: an Inuit is a member of an Arctic people

explanation.surface: An Arctic native senses the cold without being told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retains' puts T inside INUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To intuit is to understand by intuition, without conscious reasoning.

clue.text: Marsupial so quiet climbing on the whole?

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means sitting above the next piece
climbing in a down entry means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: P, from piano, means quiet in music
the sum is the whole amount

explanation.surface: A silent animal going up a tree, a question of totality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses SO P to POS, placed 'on' SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A possum is a tree-dwelling marsupial of Australasia; the American opossum is too.

clue.text: One singing in reverential tones

indicators.note: in shows the answer is sitting inside the words reverential tones

explanation.surface: A chorister singing with hushed devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the answer inside reverentiAL TOnes.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with the voice range above tenor, below soprano.

clue.text: Retinue try very hard without leader

indicators.note: without leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: to strain is to make a great effort

explanation.surface: An entourage struggling hard with no one in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without leader' removes the S from STRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A train is the body of attendants following an important person.

clue.text: One constituent is in bar supporting both parties

indicators.note: in says these pieces go inside the word for bar

parts.note: to ban is to bar
I is the Roman numeral one
a part is a constituent

explanation.surface: A voter in a pub declares support for both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the containment signal; 'constituent' suggests a voter but means a component.
explanation.definitionFit: Bipartisan means involving or backed by two political parties.

clue.text: A container is slightly open

parts.note: a jar is a container

explanation.surface: A jar's lid has been left loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajar describes a door or lid left a little way open.

clue.text: Target girl carrying nothing

indicators.note: carrying means the girl word holds the nothing letter

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A young woman with empty hands is aimed at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts O inside GAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal is an aim or objective one strives toward.

clue.text: Argued violently about foolish person's appreciation of kindness

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go round the fool
violently signals that the letters of argued are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a tit is a fool in British slang

explanation.surface: A heated quarrel over whether a fool showed thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violently' rearranges ARGUED to GRAUDE, which goes 'about' TIT. TIT is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratitude is thankfulness felt for a favour received.

clue.text: Call round

explanation.surface: Phone and visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ring means both a telephone call and a circular band or shape.
